content:
ABG Trading faces significant challenges in its port operations, including heavy reliance on manual
processes, underutilization of modern technology, and a lack of standardized workflows. These issues
result in inefficiencies, errors, and limited visibility ac ross the supply chain. Manual documentation of
weighment records, gate passes, and delivery challans creates delays, while the absence of real -time
integration with SAP leads to inaccuracies in invoicing and shipment tracking. Additionally,
inconsistencies in processes from vessel discharge to the point of sale, coupled with pilferage risks and
insufficient compliance mechanisms, further complicate operations.
To address these challenges, Axestrack proposes implementing its flagship solution, Connected Port
Logistics (CPL). CPL is a unified digital platform designed to streamline port logistics by automating key
touchpoints, digitizing documentation, and integrating real -time data into SAP. The solution includes
features such as automated token generation, w eighment slip management, and delivery challans,
reducing reliance on manual inputs and paperwork. It enhances operational transparency by creating a
comprehensive digital audit trail and leverages analytics for process optimization.
CPL will standardize w orkflows across stages, improve compliance with digital validation checkpoints,
and enable real-time tracking of coal shipments. This not only minimizes pilferage risks but also ensures
faster and more accurate invoicing. By integrating seamlessly with SAP, CPL provides ABG Trading with
a scalable, efficient, and reliable solution, enabling measurable improvements in staff productivity and
operational efficiency. This transformation will position ABG Trading as a leader in adopting advanced
digital solutions for port operations.
The implementation of Axestrack’s CPL will directly address ABG Trading’s technological, process related, and people -centric challenges. It will digitize and streamline the entire port -to-point-of-sale
workflow, ensure real -time data integration with SAP, and establish a secure, efficient, and auditable
system for managing coal shipments. This alignment ensures long -term operational excellence and a
sustainable competitive advantage for ABG Trading.

content:
CPL will address the core requirements of ABG Trading by providing the following functionalities:
• Vessel Discharge Flow
o Capture vessel discharge details, including discharges at berth or mid-sea locations.
o Record barge/truck details with timestamps and photographic evidence at key stages:
▪ When trucks load goods at the berth/jetty.
▪ When trucks unload goods at the designated plot.
o Allow users to upload discharge summary pictures for better accountability.
• Delivery Order Flow
o Enable recording and management of delivery orders at the time of sale.
• Digital Token Management
o Assign a unique digital token for each truck.
o Include details such as truck ID, DO reference, customer reference, time of arrival, and
other relevant information.
• Weighment Slip Management
o Record weight data for each truck post-weighment at the bridge.
o Generate digital weighment slips that can be printed or emailed.
• Gate Pass Management
o Capture gate pass details created by the CHA, including truck and weighment data.
o Send these details to SAP for further processing.
• Delivery Challan Creation
o Automatically generate delivery challans based on weighment and token data.
o Include key information like DC number, date, vehicle number, transport document,
weight, price, and amount.
o Send delivery challan details to SAP for seamless integration.
• Assigning User as per Segregation of Duties (Roles and Permissions)
o Port Operators: Capture and manage tokens, weighment slips, gate pass records, and
delivery challans. Access restricted to data specific to their assigned port.
o Admin Users: Manage user groups, master data, and transactional data.
o Business Users: Access SAP for invoice management and the application for real -time
discharge and delivery data.
• Executing CPL Development and Deployment
• Executing System Integration Testing (SIT) and facilitate User Acceptance Testing (UAT)
• Post Go-live Hypercare Support (1 Month)
• Key User Training through Train the Trainer approach

2. A leading conglomerate in the food and agricultural sector specializing in palm oil production
faced challenges in maintaining oil quality during transit, ETA management, automated
sequencing and optimizing in-plant operations
Project
Scope
• Real-time vehicle movement monitoring through GPS -based tracking for
transparency and efficiency.
• ETA calculation and sharing to provide unloading staff with real -time updates,
enhancing planning and resource allocation.
• Automate sequencing and prioritize delayed vehicles to reduce TAT
• Maintain unloading order through FIFO system, ensuring smooth operations.
Business
Challenges
• Product quality degradation occurred due to delays in transit and unloading,
which affected the freshness of palm fruit.
• Inefficient in-plant operations arose from challenges in adhering to th e vehicle
FIFO system for material unloading.
• A lack of visibility resulted from inadequate real -time tracking and the absence
of timely ETA communication to unloading staff.
• Delayed decision -making was caused by manual prioritization of delayed
vehicles, leading to inefficiencies in the process.
Solution
Highlights
• Continuous monitoring of vehicles was achieved through real -time GPS
tracking, ensuring visibility throughout transit.
• ETA notifications automatically informed unloading staff of vehicle arrivals
based on real-time tracking, enhancing preparedness.
• Delay management dynamically prioritized delayed vehicles, reducing the
impact on palm oil quality.
• Automated sequencing adjusted the unloading order based on vehicle status
and delays, streamlining operations.
Benefits
Delivered
• Enhanced Quality: Maintained palm oil freshness by minimizing delays.
• Operational Efficiency: Reduced in-plant TAT through automated processes.
• Improved Visibility: Real-time updates enhanced coordination between transit
and in-plant teams.
• Optimized Decision -Making: Automated prioritization reduced manual
intervention and errors.
Delivery
Process
• Engaged with client stakeholders to understand pain points & operational goals.
• Developed a tailored solution integrating client ERP, GPS tracking & automated
sequencing.
• Deployed GPS trackers, integrated ETA systems, and set up automated
workflows for prioritization.
• Ensured solution accuracy and reliability through end-to-end testing.
• Trained client staff to use the system effectively and provided post implementation support.

section_title: Our Understanding of ABG Trading Business Process
breadcrumb: Project Overview > Our Understanding of ABG Trading Business Process
content:
ABG Trading faces significant challenges in its port operations, including heavy reliance on manual processes, underutilization of modern technology, and a lack of standardized workflows. These issues result in inefficiencies, errors, and limited visibility across the supply chain. Manual documentation of weighment records, gate passes, and delivery challans creates delays, while the absence of real-time integration with SAP leads to inaccuracies in invoicing and shipment tracking. Additionally, inconsistencies in processes from vessel discharge to the point of sale, coupled with pilferage risks and insufficient compliance mechanisms, further complicate operations.

To address these challenges, Axestrack proposes implementing its flagship solution, Connected Port Logistics (CPL). CPL is a unified digital platform designed to streamline port logistics by automating key touchpoints, digitizing documentation, and integrating real-time data into SAP. The solution includes features such as automated token generation, weighment slip management, and delivery challans, reducing reliance on manual inputs and paperwork. It enhances operational transparency by creating a comprehensive digital audit trail and leverages analytics for process optimization.

CPL will standardize workflows across stages, improve compliance with digital validation checkpoints, and enable real-time tracking of coal shipments. This not only minimizes pilferage risks but also ensures faster and more accurate invoicing. By integrating seamlessly with SAP, CPL provides ABG Trading with a scalable, efficient, and reliable solution, enabling measurable improvements in staff productivity and operational efficiency. This transformation will position ABG Trading as a leader in adopting advanced digital solutions for port operations.

The implementation of Axestrack’s CPL will directly address ABG Trading’s technological, process-related, and people-centric challenges. It will digitize and streamline the entire port-to-point-of-sale workflow, ensure real-time data integration with SAP, and establish a secure, efficient, and auditable system for managing coal shipments. This alignment ensures long-term operational excellence and a sustainable competitive advantage for ABG Trading.

CPL will address the core requirements of ABG Trading by providing the following functionalities:

Vessel Discharge Flow

Capture vessel discharge details, including discharges at berth or mid-sea locations.

Record barge/truck details with timestamps and photographic evidence at key stages:

When trucks load goods at the berth/jetty.

When trucks unload goods at the designated plot.

Allow users to upload discharge summary pictures for better accountability.

Delivery Order Flow

Enable recording and management of delivery orders at the time of sale.

Digital Token Management

Assign a unique digital token for each truck.

Include details such as truck ID, DO reference, customer reference, time of arrival, and other relevant information.

Weighment Slip Management

Record weight data for each truck post-weighment at the bridge.

Generate digital weighment slips that can be printed or emailed.

Gate Pass Management

Capture gate pass details created by the CHA, including truck and weighment data.

Send these details to SAP for further processing.

Delivery Challan Creation

Automatically generate delivery challans based on weighment and token data.

Include key information like DC number, date, vehicle number, transport document, weight, price, and amount.

Send delivery challan details to SAP for seamless integration.

Assigning User as per Segregation of Duties (Roles and Permissions)

Port Operators: Capture and manage tokens, weighment slips, gate pass records, and delivery challans. Access restricted to data specific to their assigned port.

Admin Users: Manage user groups, master data, and transactional data.

Business Users: Access SAP for invoice management and the application for real-time discharge and delivery data.

section_title: As-Is Process – Export and Import Operations
breadcrumb: Business Requirements Summary > As-Is Process – Export and Import Operations
content:
Currently, logistics operations at Adani Ennore Port are largely manual and supported by multiple standalone
systems without a unified workflow. In the export process, before a vehicle arrives at the gate, a Port Entry Permit
(PEP) is expected to be created in the ITUP system. If the PEP is not pre-created, the vehicle enters the parking
area and generates the P EP through a kiosk available onsite. Simultaneously, the N4 Navis system provides
vehicle and container details. In parallel, another system called Universal Sealing System captures seal details
and vehicle images from multiple angles. All these details are printed and submitted physically to the customs
officer for review and approval. In certain cases, customs may grant partial approval, allowing the vehicle to exit
the parking area but restricting it from loading material  to the vessel until re-verification and final approval is
completed.
Once final approval is granted, the vehicle enters the port and terminal gate, completes unloading, and exits the
port, concluding the export process. The import process follows a similar flow where trucks enter the parking
area with an already generated P EP and proceed to the terminal for loading. Post service, customs officers

entry/exit, port gate entry/exit, terminal entry/exit  and port entry/exit. These integrations will enable automated
timestamp capture and real-time vehicle movement tracking. The system will provide stage-wise visibility of each
vehicle within the port lifecycle, improving turnaround time monitoring, congestion management, SLA adherence,
and data-driven decision-making. Overall, the proposed solution transforms the current manual and fragmented
operations into a fully integrated, transparent, and scalable digital ecosystem.

Hardware Warranty & AMC

Terms and Conditions

Standard Warranty Coverage

All installed hardware will carry a Standard One-Year OEM Warranty from the date the equipment is unpacked and the seal is broken, marking its readiness for installation and operational use. As per OEM policy, the hardware warranty period begins once the equipment is unpacked and the seal is broken, as it is then considered commissioned for operational use. Accordingly, we will consider the warranty start date from the point when the hardware is opened from its original packaging and made ready for installation. This includes coverage for hardware malfunction, firmware issues, and initial configuration defects, provided the equipment has been used under prescribed operating conditions.

Inclusions Under Standard Warranty

The following are covered:

Hardware faults due to manufacturing defects

Firmware issues or embedded software malfunctions

Initial configuration or calibration problems

Functional issues arising under normal operating environments

Exclusions from Warranty

The standard warranty will not cover:

Physical damage, dents, or broken components

Burnt devices due to electrical surges or short circuits

Waterlogging, corrosion, or environmental damage

Vandalism, unauthorized repairs, or tampering with device internals

These are standard OEM warranty terms and cannot be altered.

Post-Warranty Support via AMC

After the one-year warranty period, support will only be provided under an Annual Maintenance Contract (AMC). The AMC scope and pricing will be governed by the terms outlined in the final commercial agreement.

AMC Coverage

The AMC will include:

Functional support and repair for eligible hardware components

Preventive maintenance checks (if opted)

Firmware updates and remote diagnostics (where applicable)

AMC Exclusions

AMC will not include the following:

Replacement due to physical/environmental damage

Reinstallation caused by infrastructure changes (e.g., shifting or rewiring)

Repairs of third-party equipment not supplied by Axestrack

Component Availability & Obsolescence

In case any component becomes obsolete during AMC, the client will be informed. Equivalent or upgraded components (if available) will be proposed separately at additional cost.

Support SLAs

Response and resolution times will follow the SLA guidelines mutually agreed in the commercial contract, depending on equipment type and issue category.

Site Access & Client Obligations

breadcrumb: Business Requirements > Business Need and Why?
content:
Adani Kattupalli Port handles a large and diverse mix of containerized, liquid, and loose cargo. Current gate operations are semi-manual, with multiple checkpoints across Main Gate, New/Old Gate Complexes, Parking Yard, CFS, and Liquid Cargo gates. This leads to delays, increased turnaround time (TAT), security risks, and lack of real-time visibility.

To support Adani’s growth and customer service commitments, a future-ready RFID and IoT-based Gate Operation System (GOS) is needed. The system must:

Automate vehicle validation and gate operations

Integrate seamlessly with ITUP, IPOS, and Navis N4 for container and cargo workflows

Provide real-time dashboards, audit logs, and MIS for end-to-end trip visibility

Enhance safety, compliance, and operational efficiency

Manual dependency at multiple gates increases TAT and causes congestion.

Limited integration between gate operations and TOS/booking applications results in data duplication and errors.

Lack of real-time visibility of truck movement across Export, Import, CFS, and Liquid flows creates planning inefficiencies.

Ineffective threshold control allows excess trucks inside the terminal, leading to yard congestion.

Inconsistent compliance checks (PUC, insurance, vehicle fitness) create security and regulatory risks.

Limited reporting & analytics restrict management’s ability to track performance and optimize cost.

breadcrumb: Business Requirements > Solution Alignment to deliver Value
content:
The Connected Port Logistics (CPoL) solution is aligned with Adani’s digital transformation objectives by delivering a comprehensive, integrated gate automation platform that ties hardware, software, and enterprise applications into a seamless ecosystem.

End-to-End Process Coverage

Deployment of RFID readers, ANPR cameras, boom barriers, LED displays, and CCTV across all operational gates: Main Gate, New Gate Complex, Old Gate Complex, Parking Yard, CFS Gate, and Liquid Pass Gate.

Each gate is mapped in the Gate Operation System (GOS) with Location ID, Lane ID, Device IDs, and IP mapping to ensure reliable gate-level visibility.

Seamless System Integration

ITUP ↔ GOS (JSON APIs): Master synchronization of Port Entry Permits (PEP), Vehicle–RFID mapping, and GP indent types.

Hardware readiness: RFID, Camera, LED Display, lane controllers, and boom barriers connected to GOS.

GOS ↔ IPOS-NC (JSON APIs): Real-time gate validation (tag number, lane ID, GP type).

GOS ↔ Navis N4 (XML APIs): Import/Export container milestones posted as Gate Events, CT Gate Events, and RTG Events.

RDT Server (TCP Port 3590): Integration for manual boom-up requests with operator ID and reason logging.

mParivahan (REST APIs): Vehicle compliance checks for PUC, fitness, and insurance before gate clearance.

POS/UPI systems: Gate/parking fee validation integrated into GOS prior to boom opening.

Dashboards: Consolidation of all gate events, parking occupancy, congestion thresholds, and exception alerts.

SIT/UAT cycles: Validation of interfaces under live traffic conditions.

Real-Time Visibility & Control

A centralized dashboard provides lane-wise visibility, transaction timestamps, queue length, parking yard occupancy, and container milestones.

Configurable threshold controls (per gate/per lane) prevent congestion by restricting boom opening once terminal occupancy exceeds pre-defined limits.

Telemetry feeds from RFID readers, boom barriers, and cameras enable proactive maintenance and SLA monitoring.

Efficiency & Security

Performance: RFID/ANPR-based authentication ensures gate clearance in <5 seconds per vehicle

Security: End-to-end encryption, token-based API authentication, and RBAC for RDT/manual overrides.

Reliability: Redundant readers, dual power supply (UPS-backed), and automated retry with event idempotency guarantee uptime and data integrity.

Auditability: Every transaction is logged with vehicle number, tag ID, lane ID, timestamp, decision, and operator action (if applicable).

Value Creation

content:

Reduced manual interventions: Automated validations and integrated milestone logging cut down dependency on manual checks.

Compliance assurance: Integration with mParivahan and audit trails minimize regulatory risk.

Future-proof scalability: Modular, API-first architecture scales to 2× current traffic volume without performance degradation.

The proposed RFID-based Gate Operation System (GOS), integrated with Connected Port Logistics, will deliver:

Gate Automation

Vehicle authentication using RFID readers and optional ANPR cameras.

LED displays for driver guidance at entry/exit lanes.

Process Coverage

Export & Import flows: Main Gate, Parking Yard, New Gate, Old Gate.

CFS operations: Gate In/Gate Out transactions with IPOS sync.

Liquid Cargo operations: Gate In/Gate Out validations integrated with IPOS Liquid module.

System Features

Configurable threshold control to prevent excess trucks entering terminals.

Automatic alerts for overstays, wrong vehicle entry, and exception handling.

Real-time dashboards for gate operators, control tower, and management.

MIS and analytics: TAT, gate logs, parking occupancy, cargo type-wise flow.

Integration Scope

ITUP: Vehicle, RFID Tag, and GP Indent sync.

IPOS: Gate validations for Dry Cargo, CFS, and Liquid Cargo.

Navis N4: Container gate entry/exit milestone updates.

RDT Server: Manual boom-up requests (TCP).

mParivahan: Vehicle compliance validation (fitness, insurance, PUC).

POS/UPI systems: Parking/gate fee collections.

Civil & Electrical Works Scope

Execution of minor civil works such as pole and boom barrier foundation, cable trenching from pole to junction box, and preparation for LAN/Wi-Fi connectivity.

Installation of enclosures, junction boxes, and associated electrical terminations at designated gate locations.

Power and LAN/Wi-Fi connectivity up to the termination end point (junction box) shall be provided and made ready by Adani Port, ensuring network and power availability at designated locations. From the junction box onward, all internal cabling and connections for pole-mounted devices will be executed by Axestrack.

All works will be executed through a client-approved or recommended agency/vendor, adhering to Adani’s quality and safety standards.

Execution Methodology:

Activities will follow a client-defined quality checklist and be verified jointly during site readiness sign-off.

The executing vendor shall provide warranty/guarantee documentation for completed works.

Hardware installation and commissioning will be carried out by Axestrack post completion of civil and electrical readiness.

The proposed Connected Port Logistics (CPoL) – RFID Gate Automation System (GOS) at Adani Kattupalli will deliver a comprehensive, integrated, and automated gate management platform that streamlines entry/exit operations for Import, Export, CFS, Dry Cargo and Liquid Cargo flows.

The solution leverages RFID readers, ANPR cameras, boom barriers, LED displays, Kiosk Printer, Handheld RFID Readers, Industrial grade Tablet and CCTV (Smart Cameras), combined with seamless API integration with ITUP, IPOS, and Navis N4, ensuring secure, efficient, and transparent cargo movement across the port.

Note - Remote boom barrier operation through the Web/tablet interface is part of the proposed solution.

General Flow:

Main Gate In → Parking Yard → New Gate In → Old Gate In → Stack Yard (Pickup) → Old Gate Out → New Gate Out → Main Gate Out

Validation points: Main Gate In, Parking Yard (Plaza), New Gate In, Old Gate In, Old Gate Out, New Gate Out, Main Gate Out.

Navis N4 Integration: Import milestone logged when container is picked up at yard. We plan to integrate with Navis N4 via API to capture container movement events (truck loading/unloading at the yard). This milestone will then be validated at the Old Gate Complex, enabling a single-window view of container status across systems. If required, this integration-based milestone can be excluded.

Control features: Threshold truck entry at New Gate & Old Gate and can be configured as per Adani’s requirements; compliance checks before Main Gate Out.

Outcome: Secure pickup validation, reduced dwell time, real-time trip visibility.

General Flow:

Main Gate In → Parking Yard → New Gate In → Old Gate In → Stack Yard (Drop) → Old Gate Out → New Gate Out → Main Gate Out

Validation points: Same as Import (all gates).

Navis N4 Integration: Export milestone logged when container is dropped at yard. For export flow, we plan to integrate with Navis N4 via API to capture the milestone when the container is dropped at the yard (truck unloading event). This event will be validated at the Old Gate Complex, ensuring a unified single-window view of export container status. If required, this milestone can be excluded from integration.

Control features: Parking Yard monitoring to avoid premature entry, congestion control at New Gate.

Outcome: Faster export clearance, automated milestone logging, minimized manual checks.

Modified Flow:

Main Gate In → CFS Gate In → CFS Gate Out → Main Gate Out

Additional Gate Checks:

CFS Gate In/Out with RFID readers and IPOS/ ITPU sync for loose cargo validation.

Integration: CFS transactions logged in IPOS, milestones tracked separately from containerized cargo.

Control features: Traffic lights and boom barrier control for wrong vehicle exit.

Outcome: Transparent CFS cargo handling, accurate in/out logging, improved yard visibility.

Simplified Flow:

Main Gate In → Liquid Pass Gate In → Unload/Load (Manual) → Liquid Pass Gate Out → Main Gate Out

Gate Checks:

RFID validation at Main Gate In, Liquid Pass In/Out (3 Bidirectional Gates), Unload/Load point via Handheld RFID Readers (Manual input) and Main Gate Out.

Integration: IPOS and ITUP Liquid Cargo sync for tanker unloading milestones.

Compliance: mParivahan checks (PUC, insurance, fitness) enforced before unloading.

Outcome: Fast tanker turnaround, minimized congestion, automated milestone reporting for safety-critical cargo.

content:

breadcrumb: Proposed Solution > Our Understanding of AM/NS Business Process > Problem Statement
content:
AMNS operates an integrated steel plant at Hazira, Surat, which is currently undergoing a major capacity expansion aimed at nearly doubling its production capacity. Earlier, all finished goods dispatches were centrally managed through a common marshalling yard, enabling controlled vehicle movement and centralized traffic coordination. As part of the expansion initiative, the central marshalling yard has been dismantled, and dispatch operations have been decentralized. Individual production units such as CRM-1, CRM-2, HRM, and other departments now manage dispatches independently through dedicated warehouses located adjacent to their manufacturing facilities.

This decentralization has resulted in a substantial increase in internal vehicular traffic without any corresponding enhancement in road infrastructure. The impact is most pronounced in the CRM-1 zone, which experiences severe congestion during peak hours—particularly in the evening during shift changes when employee movement overlaps with commercial vehicle traffic. In addition to increased traffic volume, CRM-1 also faces challenges related to poor vehicle discipline at loading points. Incoming trucks often park in unauthorized areas, including active traffic lanes, further aggravating congestion and creating safety risks. Moreover, vehicles are frequently required to reverse into loading bays, increasing the likelihood of accidents due to blind spots and limited maneuvering space. In the recent past, multiple near-miss incidents have been reported in this area, highlighting the urgent need for improved traffic control, parking discipline, and safer loading practices within the plant.

breadcrumb: Proposed Solution > Our Understanding of AM/NS Business Process > Key Challenges
content:
Uncontrolled increase in internal vehicular traffic due to decentralized dispatch operations without corresponding road infrastructure upgrades

Severe congestion in critical zones (especially CRM-1) during peak hours caused by the overlap of employee movement and commercial vehicle dispatches

Unauthorized parking of trucks near loading areas, including on active traffic lanes, leading to traffic bottlenecks and safety risks

Unsafe vehicle maneuvering practices, particularly reversing into loading bays, increasing blind-spot and collision hazards

Rising safety exposure, evidenced by multiple near-miss incidents involving vehicles and personnel in recent months

Lack of centralized traffic monitoring and enforcement, resulting in poor vehicle discipline and inconsistent adherence to safety protocols

To address the growing internal traffic congestion and safety risks at the AMNS Hazira plant, Axestrack has conducted a detailed on-ground assessment by visiting the facility and engaging with key stakeholders across operations and logistics. Based on this assessment, Axestrack proposes the deployment of its Connected Plant Logistics (CPL) platform, a comprehensive, AI-powered solution designed to optimize internal traffic flow, enhance safety, and bring centralized visibility across decentralized dispatch operations.

The CPL platform leverages a smart grid of hardware devices, intelligent traffic logic, and advanced analytics to regulate vehicle movement inside the plant in real time. By dynamically managing traffic at critical junctions, loading bays, and high-risk zones such as CRM-1, the platform ensures smoother vehicle flow, enforces discipline, minimizes unsafe maneuvers, and significantly reduces safety hazards. The solution not only addresses current operational challenges but also creates a data-driven foundation for continuous improvement in plant logistics and traffic planning.

section_title: Smart Traffic Regulation at Plant Tri-Junctions & Choke Points
breadcrumb: Proposed Solution > To-be Process > Smart Traffic Regulation at Plant Tri-Junctions & Choke Points
content:
CPL deploys intelligent traffic management units at critical tri-junctions and intersections inside the steel plant, especially near CRM-1 and dispatch corridors. Each junction is equipped with smart cameras, traffic controllers, and AI-based decision logic that continuously monitors vehicle movement across all incoming and outgoing lanes.

The system dynamically regulates traffic by prioritizing lanes based on real-time conditions such as peak shift hours, congestion levels, vehicle type (commercial vs employee transport), and vehicle reversal at loading bay. Unlike fixed traffic signals, CPL adapts signal timing and lane permissions automatically based on live data.

Advantages

Smoothens traffic flow during peak shift change hours

Prevents congestion spillover across plant.

Reduces manual traffic intervention by security personnel

Improves overall throughput without modifying road infrastructure

breadcrumb: Proposed Solution > To-be Process > Dynamic Zone Access & Vehicle Throttling
content:
CPL enforces controlled entry into sensitive or high-traffic zones such as CRM-1 by dynamically limiting the number of vehicles allowed at any given time. Cameras and access logic track how many vehicles are already present and automatically permit or restrict new entries via traffic regulations based on predefined safety and capacity thresholds.

This ensures that traffic inside constrained areas remain within manageable limits and prevents sudden surges caused by uncoordinated vehicular movement.

Advantages

Eliminates overloading of narrow or high-risk internal roads

Maintains safe vehicle density in CRM-1 and similar zones

Reduces gridlocks caused by simultaneous vehicle arrivals

Brings discipline and predictability to vehicular movements

section_title: AI-Based Reversal Safety at Loading Bays
breadcrumb: Proposed Solution > To-be Process > AI-Based Reversal Safety at Loading Bays
content:
At loading bays, CPL deploys smart cameras with AI-based human and vehicle detection, integrated with PA systems. When a vehicle enters reverse mode for loading, the system continuously scans blind spots and the surrounding area for any manpower movement or obstruction.

If a safety risk is detected, the system immediately provides audio alerts to the driver and notifies nearby personnel, guiding the driver to stop or adjust movement until the area is clear.

Advantages

Significantly reduces blind-spot related accidents and near-misses

Protects shop-floor personnel during reversing operations

Provides real-time guidance instead of post-incident reporting

breadcrumb: Proposed Solution > To-be Process > Unauthorized Parking & Lane Obstruction Detection
content:
CPL continuously monitors internal plant lanes using smart cameras installed at fixed intervals. The AI engine identifies vehicles parked in unauthorized areas, or active traffic lanes and instantly flags these violations.

Real-time alerts are pushed to the safety and operations teams, enabling immediate corrective action before congestion or safety incidents escalate.

Advantages

Prevents blockage of main traffic corridors

Improves vehicle discipline near loading and waiting areas

Enables faster response by safety and security teams

Reduces secondary congestion caused by illegal parking

section_title: End-to-End Traffic Visibility & Control Dashboard (+1 more)
breadcrumb: Proposed Solution > To-be Process > End-to-End Traffic Visibility & Control Dashboard
content:
End-to-End Traffic Visibility & Control Dashboard: All traffic data from junctions, loading bays, and plant roads is consolidated into a centralized CPL dashboard. Safety and logistics teams get real-time visibility into vehicle movement, congestion hotspots, violations, and abnormal patterns.

This allows proactive traffic control instead of reactive incident handling.

Advantages

Single source of truth for plant traffic operations

Faster incident detection and resolution

Improved coordination between logistics, safety, and operations teams

Enables informed decision-making during peak or emergency situations

Vehicle Traceability & Predictive Analytics: CPL records detailed movement data such as vehicle entry/exit time, dwell time at particular stretch, route taken, and congestion patterns. This historical data is analysed to identify recurring bottlenecks, unsafe zones, and peak traffic trends.

Over time, this enables AMNS to fine-tune dispatch schedules, traffic rules, and infrastructure planning.

Advantages

Data-driven optimization of dispatch and traffic planning

Continuous improvement of safety inside the plant

Supports future capacity expansion planning

Moves traffic management from reactive to predictive

Advantages
• Significantly reduces blind-spot related accidents and near-misses
• Protects shop-floor personnel during reversing operations
• Provides real-time guidance instead of post-incident reporting

breadcrumb: Proposed Solution > To-be Process > Unauthorized Parking & Lane Obstruction Detection
content:
CPL continuously monitors internal plant lanes using smart cameras installed at fixed intervals. The AI
engine identifies vehicles parked in unauthorized areas, or active traffic lanes and instantly flags these
violations.
Real-time alerts are pushed to the safety and operations teams, enabling immediate corrective action
before congestion or safety incidents escalate.
Advantages
• Prevents blockage of main traffic corridors
• Improves vehicle discipline near loading and waiting areas
• Enables faster response by safety and security teams
• Reduces secondary congestion caused by illegal parking

breadcrumb: Proposed Solution > To-be Process > End-to-End Traffic Visibility & Control Dashboard
content:
All traffic data from junctions, loading bays, and plant roads is consolidated into a centralized CPL
dashboard. Safety and logistics teams get real-time visibility into vehicle movement, congestion hotspots,
violations, and abnormal patterns.
This allows proactive traffic control instead of reactive incident handling.
Advantages
• Single source of truth for plant traffic operations
• Faster incident detection and resolution
• Improved coordination between logistics, safety, and operations teams
• Enables informed decision-making during peak or emergency situations

breadcrumb: Proposed Solution > To-be Process > Vehicle Traceability & Predictive Analytics
content:
CPL records detailed movement data such as vehicle entry/exit time, dwell time at particular stretch,
route taken, and congestion patterns. This historical data is analysed to identify recurring bottlenecks,
unsafe zones, and peak traffic trends.

Over time, this enables AMNS to fine-tune dispatch schedules, traffic rules, and infrastructure planning.
Advantages
• Data-driven optimization of dispatch and traffic planning
• Continuous improvement of safety inside the plant
• Supports future capacity expansion planning
• Moves traffic management from reactive to predictive

breadcrumb: Proposed Solution > Our Understanding of AM/NS Business Process > As-is Process
content:
AM/NS currently manages its entire logistics in plant operations manually right from parking in to the gate
out of the vehicle after loading. The process begins with getting the daily dispatch plans from sales team.
After deciding on the dispatch plan, the plan will be shared with the respective transporters for the
alignment of the vehicles. Once vehicle is assigned, vehicle reaches the parking area and waits there
until the entire process of document verification at the plant gate. The security personnel at the main gate
verifies the documents and driver and vehicle manually and issue a gate pass. Once the gate pass is
issued the driver goes to the transport office and gets the DO copy and proceeds to the loading point.
The supervisor at the loading point loads the vehicle based on the loading sheet received from the
transport office and clears the vehicle once the loading is done. In this process, he performs the manual
checklist to validate the vehicle healthiness and l oaded material details. Once the vehicle is loaded it
goes to the weighbridge and then to gate out. At the main gate, the security personnel again validate the
vehicle and material loaded on it manually and allows the vehicle to pass.
Key Challenges in As-is process:
• Unauthorized access to the parking leading to heavy congestion.
• Paper-driven checks cause inconsistency in PPE/fitness/vehicle and load safety controls.
• Congestion and long dwell times increase exposure to moving equipment, noise, and emissions.
• Heavy reliance on manual processes at all the levels of the process leading to the errors.
• Multiple handoffs and delays encourage rushing and workarounds.
• Higher Turn-around times.
• Lower productivity of resources because of manual intervention.
• Lack of co-ordination and communication with stakeholders.

breadcrumb: Proposed Solution > Our Understanding of AM/NS Business Process > To-be Process (Proof of Concept)
content:
To mitigate the above risks, we propose implementing the “Connected Plant Logistics” Solution. This
solution not only provide real time control on the processes at each stage of the process but also helps
to mitigate the safety hazards related to the unauthorized movement of vehicles and its drivers in and out
of the plant. It facilitates the staff at the parking gate to allow only authorized vehicles inside the parking
reducing the congestion and safety hazards associated with that. It also automates the vehicle validation
process through the integration with the ULIP/Vahan and facilitates to carry out the safety checks before
vehicle enters the plant. It also allows to keep logs against every step carried out for the future audit
purposes. In addition, it also provides advanced analytics against various parameters to facilitate the
informed decision making

breadcrumb: Proposed Solution > Our Understanding of AMNS’s Requirements
content:
Currently, AMNS is handling its entire mining operations manually right from the dispatch planning till the vehicles carrying the minerals reaches the Dabuna Plant. The entire mining operations involves the coordination and exchange of information and data at real-time between various government and local stakeholders at every stage of the process. The heavy reliance on manual processes and the lack of real time communication between the fragmented work flows and data silos is creating an inefficiency in the entire process.

Key Challenges in As-is process:

Heavy reliance on manual processes at all the levels of the process.

Lack of visibility on the Turn-around time at  all the stages.

Unnecessary delays across the stages because of manual processes

Revenue losses owing to theft and pilferages.

Inefficient process flows and inaccurate data flow through the stages.

Lower productivity of resources because of manual intervention.

Lack of co-ordination and communication with stakeholders.

Proposed Solution:

To address above challenges, we propose implementing our state-of-the-art "Connected Plant Logistics" (CPL) and Track and trace solutions. These solutions automate the critical stages of the logistics processes using advanced unified digital layers. The solution will eliminate the manual processes and provide clear visibility on the entire process right from dispatch planning to the Epod. The integration directly with AMNS’s ERP system and I3MS, eliminates the need for manual data entry at various stages. Various data points across the stages will be automatically captured and pushed to the ERP and I3MS system, ensuring seamless operations and reducing the risk of human error.

The implementation of the solution will significantly reduce turnaround times, optimize resource utilization, and enhance process transparency through a robust digital layer. Real-time tracking of trucks and materials will provide end-to-end visibility, while automated systems will improve coordination between various stakeholders. Furthermore, the solution will capture comprehensive data for audits and reports, enabling AMNS to gain actionable insights and maintain a detailed operational record.

breadcrumb: Proposed Solution > Our Understanding of AMNS’s Requirements
content: Overall, the adoption of the solution will transform AMNS’s mining operations, enhancing efficiency, reducing costs, and providing a modern, automated framework for managing truck and material movements. This system will address current inefficiencies while future-proofing logistics processes for sustained operational excellence.

Request for Proposal (RFP): Steel Yard Management – Real-Time Yard Management
Solution for Steel Coils

AM/NS India is seeking proposals from qualified vendors for the design, development, and
implementation of a "Steel Yard Management" – a real-time yard management solution for steel
Coils. This solution aims to revolutionize our steel Coil inventory and logistics operations by
leveraging cutting-edge technology to enhance visibility, efficiency, and safety within our storage
yards.
The primary objective of this RFP is to select a partner capable of delivering a comprehensive,
scalable, and robust system that meets the detailed requirements outlined herein. We are looking
for an innovative solution that minimizes manual intervention, reduces operational costs, and
provides actionable insights for optimized yard management.

Currently, our steel Coil yard management relies on a combination of manual processes and
systems, leading to challenges such as:
• Limited real-time visibility into Coil locations and inventory.
• Increased time and effort for Coil retrieval and placement.
• Higher risk of misplacement or damages of steel Coils.
• Difficulties in tracking aging inventory and ensuring compliance.
The Steel Yard Management solution will address these pain points by introducing a digital, realtime, and intelligent system to improve operational efficiency and decision-making.

The selected vendor will be responsible for the end-to-end delivery of the Steel Yard Management
solution, including but not limited to:

breadcrumb: Scope of Work > Core System Features
content:
• Real-time Positioning: Implementation of a system for real-time positioning of each steel
Coil within the yard using suitable tagging/sensor technologies (e.g., RFID, GPS, UWB).
• Steel Coil Tracking:
o Assignment of a unique ID to each steel Coil.
o Comprehensive tracking of movement history, condition, batch information, and
grade.
• Inventory Dashboard: A centralized, live dashboard providing real-time inventory updates
with advanced filtering capabilities (e.g., by grade, size, production line, aging, and status).

o ERP systems (e.g., SAP – S4 HANA).
o Logistics modules.

Alerts & Notifications: • Configuration and delivery of real-time alerts and notifications for critical events, including:
o Misplaced Coil alerts.
o Aging inventory notifications.
o Unauthorized movement detection.

Vendors should propose a robust and scalable technology stack that aligns with modern industry
best practices. vendors are encouraged to propose solution that offers superior value or capabilities.

The selected vendor will be responsible for delivering the following:
• Detailed project plan and timelines.
• System design documentation (architecture, database schema, API specifications).
• Developed and fully tested Steel Yard Management Solution.
• Integrated and supply of all hardware components (tagging, scanners, etc.) & System
connectivity (i.e. Wi-Fi / Networking etc.)
• Supply of any manpower for operation of this solution.
• Integration with specified ERP and Logistics systems.
• Comprehensive user manuals and technical documentation.
• Training for our staff on system operation and administration.
• Deployment and go-live support.
• Post-implementation support and maintenance plan.
• Inventory reconciliation to be done for Physical & System Stocks

The successful implementation of the Steel Yard Management solution is expected to yield
significant benefits, including:

• Increased Yard Visibility: Real-time insights into the location and status of every steel Coil.
• Reduction in Coil Retrieval Time: Optimized placement and accurate location data will
significantly speed up retrieval processes.
• Minimized Loss/Misplacement: Enhanced tracking and alert systems will drastically reduce
lost or misplaced inventory.
• Better Compliance & Safety: Improved adherence to storage regulations and safer yard

• Scalability: The solution should be scalable to accommodate growth and adaptable for other

section_title: Going beyond real-time visibility (unified platform for logistics)
breadcrumb: Respondent Information > Axestrack Overview > Going beyond real-time visibility (unified platform for logistics)
content:
Axestrack with its suite of products (xSwift, Connected Plant Logistics, Managed Control Tower, Connected Plant Logistics, etc.) provides state-of-the-art tracking and visibility to shippers and fleet owners.

The unified, single-pane view across all platforms facilitates rapid and informed decision-making. This connected operating system is structured into four key layers: See, Understand & Learn, and Act.

The See layer aggregates data from multiple sources, including third-party GPS/Telematics systems, 3PL providers, ERP/TMS platforms, toll systems, government portals, OEM systems, third-party SIMs, and open APIs. This data is consolidated into a comprehensive data pool via a robust integration layer.

The Understand & Learn layer leverages advanced AI and machine learning capabilities to transform this data lake into a data pool, enabling deeper insights and meaningful analytics.

The Act layer presents this processed data through unified platforms, offering actionable analytics and reports. These insights empower the Managed Control Tower to make real-time interventions, ensuring efficient operations and improved outcomes.

content:

breadcrumb: Respondent Information > Axestrack Overview > Stability with scale
content:
At Axestrack, we are more than a solution provider—we are strategic partner. With over 15 years of experience in logistics and technology, and the management of our own fleet of 200+ vehicles, we leverage our deep industry expertise to proactively analyze key business KPIs and recommend targeted solutions that address operational gaps. As a bootstrapped and profitable organization, we currently manage 2.5 lakh+ fleets and oversee lakhs of trips monthly.

Our in-house Center of Excellence (CoE) designs, develops, and deploys cutting-edge digital solutions tailored to the logistics industry. These solutions support every stage from proof of concept (POC) to full implementation and enhancement. Our unified digital logistics platform seamlessly integrates with any ERP system as a bolt-on solution, enabling faster, more efficient plant operations and driving impactful improvements across internal plant processes.

AMNS, as a leading steel manufacturer, operates extensive yards to store and handle high-value steel coils that are critical to its production and supply chain operations. Efficient yard management is essential to ensure timely dispatches, minimize operational costs, and maintain product quality. However, the current processes face several operational challenges that hinder productivity and create avoidable delays.

Lack of Real-Time Tracking: Inability to monitor the exact location and movement of coils within the yard, leading to inefficiencies.

Misplaced Coils: Difficulty in identifying misplaced coils, resulting in operational delays.

Loading Delays: Increased truck and wagon turnaround times due to untraceable coils during dispatch operations.

Coil Ageing: Ineffective inventory rotation, leading to ageing coils and potential quality concerns.

To address these challenges, Axestrack proposes an advanced Digital Yard Management Solution that leverages Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) technology and AI-powered analytics to transform AMNS’s yard operations into a streamlined, data-driven system.

breadcrumb: Executive Summary. > Option: BLE Based Solution Overview:
content:
Graphical representation:

BLE-Based Real-Time Tracking: Deployment of BLE tags on coils combined with strategically placed BLE gateways to provide precise, real-time visibility of all coils in the yard.

AI-Driven Optimization: Intelligent algorithms to suggest optimal stacking, retrieval, and dispatch plans ensuring FIFO/LIFO compliance and minimal coil movement.

Automated Misplacement Alerts: Proactive notifications to operational teams in case of misplaced or wrongly stacked coils.

Accelerated Loading Operations: Guided retrieval processes for faster and error-free truck/wagon loading, reducing turnaround time.

Centralized Yard Dashboard: Live yard maps, KPI dashboards, and actionable insights for improved operational visibility and control.

Seamless ERP Integration: Ensures smooth data exchange between the Yard Management System and AMNS’s existing ERP platforms.

breadcrumb: Executive Summary. > Option: RFID Based Solution Overview:
content:
Graphical representation:

This solution uses RFID technology to accurately identify and update the location of steel coils in the yard. The process is as follows:

Tagging the RFID with the Coil: As soon as the Quality Check (QC) of a coil is completed, the operator at the packing yard maps an RFID tag with the Unique ID of the coil using a handheld RFID and barcode reader.

C-hook Engages Coil: When the C-hook engages a coil to shift it to the yard, the RFID reader strategically mounted on the hook detects the tag and retrieves the associated Unique ID of the coil.

Capture X-Y Coordinates: As the crane moves, RFID tags and readers placed on the crane girder and its rails continuously track the X-Y movements of the crane on the yard grid. This data is sent to the central dashboard in real-time.

Movement Tracking: When the coil is placed in a new location, the same process captures the updated X-Y coordinates and updates the coil’s location on the central dashboard.

breadcrumb: Executive Summary. > Key Benefits to AMNS:
content:
40% reduction in retrieval and loading times.

Improved yard space utilization and organized stacking.

Elimination of manual searching, leading to higher labor productivity.

Minimized inventory ageing and quality risks through automated coil rotation management.

Enhanced decision-making with real-time operational insights and analytics.

section_title: Comparison BLE Vs. RFID based Solution
breadcrumb: Comparison BLE Vs. RFID based Solution
content:
#: 1 | Feature: Real time Tracking | RFID Based Solution: No (Event Based) | BLE Based Solution: Yes (Continuous tracking)
#: 2 | Feature: Accuracy | RFID Based Solution: Provides accuracy of 3-5 Mtrs | BLE Based Solution: Provides accuracy of 1 Mtrs
#: 3 | Feature: Tag Cost | RFID Based Solution: Tags are low cost | BLE Based Solution: Tags are comparatively costlier
#: 4 | Feature: Metal Interference | RFID Based Solution: Metal interference is high | BLE Based Solution: Less metal interference
#: 5 | Feature: Read range | RFID Based Solution: 10-15 Mtrs | BLE Based Solution: 80-100 Mtrs
#: 6 | Feature: Battery | RFID Based Solution: No (Passive tags) | BLE Based Solution: Yes (3 years Battery life)
#: 7 | Feature: Infrastructure cost | RFID Based Solution: Medium | BLE Based Solution: High
#: 8 | Feature: Best for | RFID Based Solution: Gate based entry/exit mapping | BLE Based Solution: Live yard mapping/digital twin, real time view

Real-Time Positioning: Axestrack will deploy a robust real-time positioning system using Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE)/RFID gateways and tags strategically placed across the yard. Each steel coil will be tagged with a BLE beacon/RFID, enabling accurate detection of its current position within the yard grid. The system ensures:

Live visibility of all coils on a digital yard map.

High precision location updates with minimal infrastructure costs compared to GPS or UWB.

Scalable architecture to cover both open and covered yard areas effectively.

Steel Coil Tracking: Each steel coil will be assigned a unique digital ID, linked to its physical BLE tag/RFID.

The system will record and maintain a complete movement history of the coil within the yard, ensuring traceability from production to dispatch.

Metadata such as batch number, grade, size, and condition will be integrated into the tracking system to provide a 360-degree view of each asset.

Inventory Dashboard: A centralized, web-based dashboard will provide real-time inventory insights, enabling operations teams to monitor and manage the yard efficiently.

Advanced filtering and search capabilities will allow users to query inventory based on grade, size, production line, coil ageing, and movement status.

KPI widgets (e.g., yard occupancy, dwell time, ageing coils) will enable data-driven decision-making and proactive yard management.
To ensure seamless operations, Axestrack’s Yard Management Solution will offer:

breadcrumb: Core System Features > Integration Capabilities > ERP Integration:
content:
ERP Integration:: The system will integrate with SAP S/4HANA and other ERP platforms through REST APIs or middleware. This will enable:

Automated data exchange (e.g., coil creation, dispatch orders).

Synchronized inventory records between the yard system and enterprise systems.

Logistics Module Integration:: Integration with logistics modules will provide visibility into inbound/outbound vehicle movements and enable real-time planning of coil loading/unloading based on dispatch schedules.

This open API architecture ensures flexibility for future integrations with warehouse, transport, and production systems.

Axestrack’s solution will incorporate a robust alerts and notifications engine, configurable for key operational events:

Misplaced Coil Alerts: Immediate notifications when a coil is stacked or moved to an unauthorized location, preventing operational delays and rework.

Aging Inventory Notifications: Automated alerts for coils exceeding predefined dwell time thresholds, ensuring FIFO/LIFO compliance and preventing quality degradation.

Unauthorized Movement Detection: Real-time alerts for any coil movement that is not part of an authorized workflow, enhancing yard security.

Notifications can be delivered via:

Mobile App push notifications for on-ground supervisors.

Email/SMS alerts for management teams.

Dashboard pop-ups for control room operators.

breadcrumb: Technical Architecture > Multi-Tenant SaaS Model on AWS
content: Our solution is built on a robust multi-tenant SaaS architecture, leveraging the scalability and security of Amazon Web Services (AWS) to deliver a high-performing and reliable platform. This architecture allows us to serve multiple customers (tenants) from a shared infrastructure while ensuring data isolation, configurability, and consistent performance.

breadcrumb: Technical Architecture > How it Works > Multi-Tenant Design
content:
Multi-Tenant Design: A single instance of the application serves multiple tenants.

Each tenant’s data is logically isolated using tenant identifiers at the database and application layers.

Shared resources such as compute, storage, and networking are optimized to support multiple users without impacting performance.

Cloud-Native Infrastructure: Deployed on AWS using services such as:

Amazon EC2/ECS/EKS for compute resources.

Amazon RDS/Aurora for database management with tenant-aware schemas.

Amazon S3 for object storage.

AWS CloudFront for global content delivery and faster load times.

AWS Cognito for secure user authentication and authorization.

AWS VPC and Security Groups for network and data security.

Scalability and High Availability: Auto-scaling groups adjust resources dynamically based on workload.

Multi-AZ deployments and load balancing ensure high availability and fault tolerance.

Customization for Tenants

Supports tenant-specific configurations like branding, workflows, and access controls while maintaining a unified codebase.

Cost Efficiency: Users benefit from a shared infrastructure model, reducing the cost of ownership compared to a single-tenant system.

Seamless Updates: All tenants receive automatic updates and enhancements without downtime or disruption.

Scalability: The architecture can scale horizontally to support growing user bases without performance degradation.

Data Security & Privacy: Each tenant’s data is logically isolated, ensuring privacy and compliance with data protection standards.

High Availability: AWS infrastructure ensures 99.99% uptime with disaster recovery capabilities, giving users uninterrupted access to the platform.

Performance Optimization: With AWS’s global presence and CDN (CloudFront), users enjoy fast response times regardless of location.

Customizability: Tenants can customize their experience within the shared application framework, from UI branding to role-based access controls.

Compliance Ready: Leveraging AWS’s compliance certifications (ISO, SOC, GDPR, etc.), our platform aligns with global regulatory requirem

section_title: Our Understanding of Apcotex’s Business Process
breadcrumb: Proposed Solution > Our Understanding of Apcotex’s Business Process
content:
The Apcotex’s outbound dispatch process is predominantly manual and lacks system integration, resulting in operational delays and limited transparency. After the dispatch plan is finalized, transporters receive intimation through email and arrange vehicles accordingly. On arrival at the plant, security personnel carry out document verification manually before granting entry. Vehicles then move to the weighbridge and loading areas where weighment, loading instructions, and related data are recorded on paper, with no connection to the SAP system. Invoicing is also performed manually, adding to processing time and increasing the risk of errors or discrepancies.

Once vehicles enter the plant, there is no digital visibility of their location or status at various stages such as waiting, loading, or post-loading checks. This makes it difficult to identify bottlenecks, track turnaround time (TAT), or monitor loading productivity. After dispatch, the absence of a unified tracking mechanism and the fragmented transporter network further result in no real-time visibility of vehicles while in transit. Similarly, for inbound movements, there is no real-time visibility of trucks carrying critical raw materials, leading to poor planning, delays in material availability, and hampered operational efficiency. Additionally, the manual checks at the gate are time-consuming, further slowing down the overall supply chain.

Key Challenges

Entirely manual gate security checks, weighbridge operations, and loading processes with no SAP integration

No digital visibility of vehicle movement or stage-wise status inside the plant, leading to hidden bottlenecks

Inability to monitor TAT, loading efficiency, or productivity in real time

Manual invoicing that prolongs processing and increases the risk of errors

Lack of real-time vehicle tracking on outbound routes due to a fragmented transporter network

No real-time visibility of inbound truck movement for critical raw materials, causing poor planning and operational inefficiencies

Lengthy and manual gate verification process that delays both inbound and outbound movements

breadcrumb: Proposed Solution > Our Understanding of Apcotex’s Business Process > To-be Process
content:
The proposed “Unified Digital Logistics Solution” replaces manual tasks with automated, real-time workflows for both outbound, inbound and in plant movements. Dispatch planning is executed on a centralized platform linked to SAP, where transporters receive dispatch schedules and upload vehicle and driver details before arrival. Pre-arrival validation checks the documents—such as driver license, vehicle fitness certificate, and insurance—against predefined rules, enabling automatic approval or flagging exceptions. Once validated, the system generates a digital gate pass and sends an entry slot confirmation to both transporter and plant security.

At the plant gate, vehicles are authenticated through RFID and Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR), drastically reducing entry time and eliminating paper-based verification. Inside the plant, IoT sensors installed strategically at various stages provide live visibility of vehicle movement across all stages—waiting, loading, and weighbridge operations. Weighbridge data flows directly to SAP, triggering automated loading confirmation and digital invoicing.

For inbound logistics, the same platform tracks raw-material trucks from source to plant and share accurate ETAs. Pre-arrival validation ensures all driver and vehicle documents are approved before gate entry, preventing delays and supporting better production planning. Real-time dashboards give operations and management teams complete oversight of TAT, bottlenecks, fleet utilization, and transporter performance, driving proactive decisions and continuous efficiency gains.

Key Benefits

Pre-Arrival Validation: Automated verification of driver and vehicle documents ensures compliance and speeds up gate entry.

End-to-End Visibility: Live tracking of inbound and outbound vehicles, both in transit and inside the plant.

SAP & Weighbridge Integration: Automated weighbridge data capture and digital invoicing reduce manual errors.

Faster Gate Operations: Digital gate passes and RFID/ANPR authentication minimize waiting time.

Optimized TAT & Planning: Accurate ETAs and real-time stage monitoring improve scheduling, inventory control, and overall productivity.

section_title: Going beyond real-time visibility (unified platform for logistics)
breadcrumb: Respondent Information > Axestrack Expertise & Recognitions > Going beyond real-time visibility (unified platform for logistics)
content:
Axestrack with its suite of products (xSwift, Connected Plant Logistics, Managed Control Tower, Connected Plant Logistics, etc.) provides state-of-the-art tracking and visibility to shippers and fleet owners.

The unified, single-pane view across all platforms facilitates rapid and informed decision-making. This connected operating system is structured into three key layers: See, Understand & Learn, and Act.

The See layer aggregates data from multiple sources, including third-party GPS/Telematics systems, 3PL providers, ERP/TMS platforms, toll systems, government portals, OEM systems, third-party SIMs, and open APIs. This data is consolidated into a comprehensive data pool via a robust integration layer.

The Understand & Learn layer leverages advanced AI and machine learning capabilities to transform this data lake into a data pool, enabling deeper insights and meaningful analytics.

The Act layer presents this processed data through unified platforms, offering actionable analytics and reports. These insights empower the Managed Control Tower to make real-time interventions, ensuring efficient operations and improved outcomes.

breadcrumb: Proposed Solution > Our Understanding of Ather Energy Business Process > As-is Process
content:
Currently, Asahi Glass India Ltd. relies heavily on manual processes for tracking pallets within and outside its plant and warehouse. These processes depend significantly on human intervention at key system touchpoints, such as gate entries, pallet movement checks, and compliance validations. This results in inefficiencies and inconsistencies across operations.

The diagram below illustrates the current As-is flow at Asahi India Glass.

The absence of standardized procedures across multiple parallel processes leads to high turnaround times (TAT), especially at the plant gate. Pallet tracking is uneven and prone to errors, contributing to an annual loss of approximately 10% of pallets. Compliance checks are insufficient across various stages, and the lack of a unified tracking system makes real-time monitoring impossible.

Additionally, excessive reliance on paperwork and administrative staff input slows down operations, creates bottlenecks, and compromises the accuracy of records. The absence of Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) further exacerbates the challenges, as productivity and process automation goals remain unmeasured and unoptimized.

breadcrumb: Proposed Solution > Our Understanding of Ather Energy Business Process > To-be Process
content:
With Axestrack's "Connected Plant Logistics" (CPL) deployed, the process will transform into a streamlined and technology-driven system. RFID readers, both static and handheld, will be installed at critical checkpoints such as gates, the pallet area, and warehouses, enabling automated and accurate pallet tracking. Each pallet will be equipped with two anti-metal RFID tags, ensuring comprehensive tracking and eliminating discrepancies.

The diagram below illustrates the To-be flow progression through various checkpoints for Asahi India Glass

Manual checks will be replaced with automated data capture and real-time updates integrated with Asahi's ERP system, providing centralized control and real-time visibility through a command center. Digitalized documentation will replace paper-based processes, significantly reducing administrative overhead. TAT will be tracked and optimized with a breakdown by process steps, allowing for bottleneck identification and resolution.

Compliance checks will become more robust and consistent across all stages, ensuring process standardization and adherence to protocols. The benefits of this transformation are significant: operational efficiency will increase with reduced TAT and bottlenecks, pallet losses will decline due to accurate tracking, and real-time visibility will enhance decision-making.

Standardized processes will ensure consistency, while automation will free up administrative staff for higher-value tasks. The deployment of CPL will provide Asahi Glass with a scalable and future-ready logistics system, delivering measurable improvements in productivity, cost savings, and overall process reliability.

Business Case – Yard Management System (YMS)
 Ashok Leyland – Alwar RSO

Objective
 Digitise yard operations at Alwar RSO (Yard 1, Yard 2 & Bus Yard) to reduce manual effort, improve retrieval efficiency, and bring full VIN-level traceability across ~4,200 vehicles.

Current Challenges
 • Only line-level parking recorded; no exact slot visibility
 • Driver memory–based retrieval across ~4,000 truck/bus slots
 • Frequent re-parking, rework movement, & yard shifting not tracked
 • Difficult VIN retrieval during FIFO dispatch
 • No real-time yard capacity view (free/occupied slots)
 • Buses move Production → RSO Yard → Bodywork Vendor → Bus Yard, with no digital trace
 • High time-to-retrieve, congestion, and unproductive labour effort

Proposed Solution – Axestrack Yard Management System
 • VIN-based digital intake & slot-level tracking (GPS/lat-long)
 • Real-time yard map for Yard 1, Yard 2, Bus Yard
 • Navigation-based retrieval for drivers
 • FIFO-based dispatch automation
 • Movement history: parking → re-parking → rework → dispatch
 • Driver/Jockey productivity analytics
 • Yard utilisation dashboards

Commercials
 • Yard 1: INR 1,35,000 per month
 • Yard 2: INR 1,35,000 per month
 Total – INR 2,70,000 per month (Bus Yard optional addition)

ROI Snapshot (Conservative Estimate)

1. Retrieval Time Savings
 • Current: 30–45 minutes per vehicle
 • Post-YMS: 5–10 minutes
 → 45–60 percent reduction
 Assuming 50–80 retrievals per day:
 20–30 labour hours saved daily
 = ₹3–4.5 lakh per month saved (driver + supervisor time)

2. Yard Utilisation Improvement
 • 15–20 percent better slot utilisation
 → Avoids overflow, improves dispatch readiness
 Estimated impact: ₹1.5–2 lakh per month (reduced re-parking, optimised flow)

3. Reduced Misplacements / Avoidable Movements
 • Eliminates duplicate movements & wrong-parked vehicles
 → ₹0.5–1 lakh per month indirect savings

4. Faster Dispatch → Faster Billing
 • 15–25 percent improvement in dispatch throughput
 → Even a 1-day reduction in billing cycle for 50–100 vehicles
 = ₹2–3 lakh per month cash-flow advantage

Total Monthly ROI Potential

₹8.5 lakh – ₹10 lakh per month
 vs.
 Subscription Cost: ₹2 lakh per month

ROI: 2.7× to 5× return within the first month.

Conclusion
 Digitising Yard 1, Yard 2 and Bus Yard through Axestrack YMS will significantly reduce operational friction, bring complete traceability, speed up dispatch cycles, and deliver a strong and measurable monthly ROI.

Business Case – Yard Management System (YMS)

Ashok Leyland – Alwar RSO

(Designed to complement existing i-Track telematics)

1. Context

Every Ashok Leyland vehicle is already equipped with i-Track for outbound visibility.
 However, i-Track does not solve internal yard-level operations, because yard movements happen in tightly packed spaces where GPS cannot show which slot a vehicle is parked in.

Therefore, Axestrack’s YMS is designed as a micro-location and workflow layer, not a replacement for i-Track.

Slot-level accuracy will be captured using:
 • Driver’s mobile app (lat-long while parking in a line)
 • Optional integration with i-Track APIs (if needed)

This reduces complexity and avoids additional hardware while giving position-level traceability.

2. Current Challenges (Not Addressed by i-Track)

• Only line-level parking known; exact slot unknown
 • Retrieval across ~4,200 vehicles (Yard 1 + Yard 2 + Bus Yard) is manual
 • Vehicles frequently re-parked for rework/space but not digitally logged
 • VIN-based FIFO dispatch becomes slow because vehicles are hard to locate
 • No yard utilisation or free-space view
 • Buses move Production → RSO Yard → Bodywork Vendor → Bus Yard, without digital tracking
 • High dependency on driver/jockey memory → inconsistent operations

3. Proposed Solution – Axestrack Yard Management System (YMS)

A lightweight, low-infrastructure, mobile-first system using driver mobile app for lat-long capture.

Key Capabilities

• VIN-based digital check-in (QC / RSO / Bodywork / Bus Yard)
 • Slot-level parking captured via driver app (lat-long stamp per drop)
 • Real-time yard map showing free vs. occupied slots
 • Navigation-based retrieval guidance
 • Re-parking, rework and cross-yard movement history
 • FIFO dispatch automation
 • Driver/Jockey productivity analytics
 • Option to integrate i-Track for single-pane visibility

4. Commercials

Yard 1 + Yard 2: INR 2,00,000 per month total
 (Bus Yard can be added at small incremental cost)

5. ROI Case (Even With i-Track Already Deployed)

1. Retrieval Time Savings

• Today: 20–45 mins per vehicle
 • With YMS (lat-long based): 5–10 mins
 → 40–60 percent reduction

At 50–80 retrievals/day:
 → 20–30 labour hours saved daily
 = ₹3–4.5 lakh per month

2. Yard Utilisation Improvement

Accurate slot mapping across 4,200+ spaces
 → 10–20 percent better utilisation
 = ₹1–2 lakh per month

3. Eliminated Misplacements

No “lost” vehicles or incorrect re-parking
 = ₹0.5–1 lakh per month

4. Faster Dispatch → Faster Billing

Reducing dispatch cycle by even 1 day:
 → ₹1–3 lakh per month value

Total Monthly ROI

₹5.5 – ₹10.5 lakh per month
 vs.
 Cost: ₹2 lakh per month

ROI = 2.7× to 5× every month

6. Why YMS Is Still Required Even With i-Track

i-Track covers inter-city telematics, whereas YMS covers:
 • Slot-level micro-location
 • Yard occupancy
 • Re-parking/rework workflows
 • Retrieval navigation
 • Queuing and dispatch optimisation
 • Yard operations productivity

Together: i-Track + YMS = Full visibility from Production → Yard → Dispatch → Dealer

content:
Ashok Leyland’s inbound logistics operations involve multiple fixed loading plants and unloading plants across India. While the current tracking platform provides en-route visibility of vehicles, it lacks plant-level integration for capturing gate-in and gate-out events. This creates:

Limited visibility of TAT: No accurate timestamps of vehicle entry and exit at plants.

Operational inefficiencies: Delay analysis is difficult without standardized TAT measurement.

Dependence on manual records: Increases scope of errors and exceptions.

Missed benchmarking opportunities: Plant-to-plant performance cannot be measured uniformly.

Business Need: To establish a standalone Connected Plant Logistics (CPL) solution that digitizes plant-level gate processes, integrates with existing Tracking Partner, and provides real-time monitoring of inbound vehicles TAT to enhance visibility, efficiency, and accountability across 8 Ashok Leyland plants

content:
The CPL solution will digitize and automate all inbound and outbound gate operations across Ashok Leyland’s 8 plants.

Automated Vehicle Identification:

Each vehicle is identified at entry/exit using RFID tags / FASTag ID / ANPR.

Tag data cross-verified against the vehicle master in CPL platform.

ULIP based verification for the RC/PUC/Insurance

Gate-In & Gate-Out Timestamping:

Automatic logging of date & time when vehicle enters or exits the plant gate.

No manual entry required, reducing human error.

TAT Computation at Gate Level:

Exit timestamp from loading plant → Entry timestamp at unloading plant.

Gate-wise performance metrics consolidated into overall Plant-to-Plant TAT.

Exception Handling:

Vehicles without valid RFID/FASTag/ANPR match flagged for manual verification.

Role-Based Gate Dashboard:

Security team: Gate event verification.

Plant operations: Queue monitoring, vehicle turnaround reports.

Central SCM team: Consolidated visibility across all plants.

MIS & Audit Trail:

Exception log (vehicles entered/exited without valid tags).

Audit trail for compliance and dispute resolution.

group_key: Yard Management Proposal Ashok LeyLand v2.docx::2.1
content:
Business Need: Yard operations currently run at scale but without position-level digital visibility (VIN tracked only by memory/line reference).

QC “Pass to Sales” → Yard → Re-park/Rework → Dispatch involves multiple movements where location/status is not reliably captured.

Bus bodywork vendor loop adds additional handoffs where traceability gaps compound.

Why This Matters Now: FIFO-based dispatch becomes slow and error-prone when exact slot/position is unknown → search loops, delays, and re-handling.

Re-parking and space corrections break the “last known location” assumption, increasing operational risk as volumes grow.

No real-time free/occupied view limits planning, causes congestion, and forces reactive yard management.

Business Impact of Current State: Increased retrieval time and dispatch slippages (missed windows, lower dispatch reliability).

Higher operational effort (extra moves, avoidable driver/jockey time, overtime).

Greater risk and inconsistency due to dependence on individual memory (audit gaps, disputes, compliance exposure).

content: The Yard Management Solution must manage all physical yard areas as a single logical Yard, providing one unified VIN inventory and search across the operation. It should digitize the complete VIN journey from QC “Pass to Sales” through yard parking, re-parking and rework movements, the bus bodywork vendor loop (gate-out/gate-in and return intake), and finally dispatch. The system must capture exact slot/position-level parking (with optional GPS/photo proof), record every movement with a full audit trail (who moved it, from–to location, timestamps, and reason), and enable FIFO-aligned dispatch readiness through picklists and guided retrieval with VIN validation. It must also provide real-time visibility of yard occupancy (free vs occupied slots), utilization and congestion, support exception handling and compliance controls, deliver operational dashboards and productivity analytics, and integrate as required with QC/ERP and dispatch planning systems (with optional linkage to outbound Track & Trace where applicable).

Full movement history and audit trail by VIN/user/time.

KPIs: retrieval TAT, dwell time, utilization, moves per VIN, jockey productivity, FIFO adherence, exceptions.

Exportable reports for shift/day/month reviews.

The digital twin is available in two complementary views:

group_key: Yard Management Proposal Ashok LeyLand v2.docx::5.4
content:
Slot View: A lane/slot-based layout that mirrors the physical yard arrangement. Each slot shows the current VIN/vehicle occupying it, enabling quick search and position-level visibility for supervisors and drivers. It also provides a real-time view of free vs occupied slots for space planning and congestion control.

Map View: A satellite/map-based view where the same lanes are represented as geofenced parking areas on the actual yard footprint. Supervisors can visually locate vehicles on the ground map, validate parking accuracy, and support navigation-based retrieval by guiding drivers to the correct lane/parking position.

Together, the two views ensure the yard inventory is always available as a single source of truth, improving parking accuracy, reducing vehicle search time during FIFO dispatch, and enabling better yard utilization and operational control.
